experiment_name: Milestone M2 Phase 11.2: Controlled 7B Prompt-Conditioning Experiment

experimental_design.question: Does an explicit contrastive instruction requiring 7B to evaluate identity mismatch + authorization state + observed HTTP result reduce benign-normalization errors without increasing false positives on controls?
experimental_design.condition_a_baseline: Current frozen Track A prompt unchanged
experimental_design.contrastive_instruction_text:
CONTRASTIVE REASONING REQUIREMENT:
Before concluding that an observed successful response is benign, explicitly check whether the requester identity, object ownership/tenant/role, and authorization relationship are consistent. Distinguish 'request succeeded' from 'request was authorized'. Use only identifiers and facts present in the supplied evidence. If the evidence does not establish an authorization mismatch, abstain rather than invent one.

vulnerable.description: Read-only invoice endpoint; 7B concludes benign session retrieval without detecting IDOR cross-tenant access
Patient records endpoint; 7B claims access restricted but ignores patient ID parameter ownership
Order refund state transition; 7B misclassifies workflow/state bypass as benign paid-state order
Document export package with multi-tenant collaboration facts; 7B drops to benign collaborator check
Cross-tenant role mutation; 7B sees admin caller without verifying target user tenant boundary

controls.description: Patched invoice details endpoint with strict ownership check
Patched patient records endpoint with patient consent check
Patched refund endpoint enforcing strict transaction state validation
Patched document export package verifying organization export permissions
Patched role assignment endpoint validating tenant-scoped role grant
